questions.prompt: Salma wants a healthy snack after school. Which one should she choose?

options.text: a doughnut
an apple
a bag of crisps
a bottle of soda

questions.explanation: An apple is a fruit, and fruits are healthy food, so it is the right snack. A doughnut is full of sugar, a bag of crisps is full of salt and oil, and a bottle of soda is full of sugar too: all three are unhealthy food, bad for the body.

questions.prompt: Your friend eats lots of sweets every day. Which sentence gives him the right advice?

options.text: You should eat lots of sweets.
You don't should eat lots of sweets.
You shouldn't eat lots of sweets.
You shouldn't to eat lots of sweets.

questions.explanation: Eating lots of sweets is a bad idea, so the advice is opened by shouldn't and the verb after it stays bare: You shouldn't eat lots of sweets. The sentence with should gives the opposite advice, the form with to after shouldn't adds a word that never follows it, and "don't should" puts an auxiliary in front of a word that already carries its own negative.

questions.prompt: The dentist tells you to brush your teeth twice a day. It is a rule, not an idea. Which sentence says it?

options.text: You must brush your teeth twice a day.
You must to brush your teeth twice a day.
You must brushing your teeth twice a day.
You mustn't brush your teeth twice a day.

questions.explanation: A rule is stated with must and a bare verb: You must brush your teeth twice a day. The form with to after must adds a word that never follows it, the -ing form cannot stand there either, and mustn't would say the opposite, that brushing your teeth is forbidden.

questions.prompt: Karim runs up to the third floor and he is not tired at the top. Which sentence about Karim is correct?

options.text: He cans run up the stairs.
He can to run up the stairs.
He can't run up the stairs.
He can run up the stairs.

questions.explanation: Karim is able to do it, so the word is can, which never adds an -s and is never followed by to: He can run up the stairs. The sentence with can't says that he is not able, and the story tells us exactly the opposite.

questions.prompt: You are writing a menu. Complete the two questions: "___ eggs do you want? ___ milk do you want?"

options.text: How much ... How many
How many ... How much
How many ... How many
How much ... How much

questions.explanation: Eggs carry an -s and you count them one by one, so the question word is How many; milk has no plural and you cannot count it one by one, so the question word is How much. It is the noun that chooses the word, which is why the two questions cannot take the same one.
